exercises.prompt: What has hands but can't clap?
exercises.explanation: A clock has hour and minute hands, but nothing to clap them with. (A watch works too.)

exercises.prompt: The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
exercises.explanation: Darkness is the classic answer: the more of it there is, the less you can see. Fog fits the wording just as well.

exercises.prompt: A woman gives birth to two boys. They have the same mother and father, were born in the same hour of the same day of the same year — yet they are not twins. How is this possible?
choices: They are two of a set of triplets
They were born in different time zones
exercises.answer: They are two of a set of triplets
exercises.explanation: Triplets (or higher multiples) are born together, so any two of them share a birth hour without being 'twins' — the trap is assuming that two simultaneous births must mean twins.

exercises.prompt: A family has exactly two children. You learn that at least one of them is a boy who was born on a Tuesday. Assuming sexes and weekdays are equally likely and independent, what is the probability that both children are boys?
exercises.explanation: Of the 196 equally likely (sex, day) combinations for two children, 27 include a Tuesday-born boy, and 13 of those have two boys. The extra detail makes the case 'both are boys' more likely than the plain 'at least one boy' answer of 1/3.

exercises.prompt: Where did domesticated guinea pigs originate?
exercises.explanation: Guinea pigs were domesticated in the Andes thousands of years ago, mainly as food. They are neither pigs nor from Guinea — a naming trap, probably from sailors' confusion over trade routes.

exercises.prompt: What colour is a polar bear's skin underneath its fur?
exercises.explanation: Polar bear skin is black, which helps absorb heat. The fur only looks white because its hollow, translucent hairs scatter light.

exercises.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
exercises.explanation: Mandarin has far more native speakers than any other language. English leads when you count all speakers, native and second-language, which is why it is the common trap.

exercises.prompt: A resting heart beats about 70 times a minute. Roughly how many times does it beat over an 80-year life?
exercises.explanation: 70 × 60 × 24 × 365 ≈ 36.8 million beats per year, and × 80 years ≈ 2.9 billion, so about 3 billion.

exercises.prompt: What begins with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
exercises.explanation: A teapot begins with T, ends with T, and has tea (T) inside it.
